column1: Before I sign off on this budget, I want someone to poke holes in it from every angle - facts, failure case, whether it's overbuilt, whether the math actually works.
We're about to approve the Q4 expansion plan and I need it stress tested hard before Friday's board call.
Can you tear into this strategy doc before I bring it to the partners? I want the worst-case argument laid out too.
This budget looks clean but I want it hit from every side - is it too much, are the numbers real, what's the case it flops.
Marketing keeps saying the campaign lifted signups 40 percent and I want that checked against the actual data before we brag about it in the board deck.
You told me the migration was done last week - I need that confirmed against something real before I tell the client it's live.
Our ops lead swears the new vendor cut costs 15 percent, but I want that run down against the invoices before I repeat it anywhere.
The report says churn dropped this quarter. Before I put that in front of investors, somebody needs to trace it back to the source.
I've got the pricing memo open and I'm about to greenlight it, but every dollar figure in here needs to trace back to where it actually came from.
This forecast has six figures on it and I'm not signing off until each one's origin is nailed down.
Before this deck goes to the investors, walk every figure back to its source so nothing gets caught out later.
There are a dozen percentages on this slide and I need to know where each one came from before I use it in the pitch.
This is the third time you've quoted a price we froze months ago - I need that to actually stop happening, not just get apologized for again.
We've been over this before about sending drafts without asking first, and it keeps slipping through, so make it stick this time.
I corrected this same formatting mistake two weeks ago and here it is again - I need a real fix, not another sorry.
You keep mixing up which account this data belongs to, and I've flagged it before. Make sure it actually holds this time.
This competitor teardown is way too big for one pass - get some people digging, someone drafting, and someone else checking it before it lands on my desk.
I need the vendor comparison researched, written up, and reviewed by a second set of eyes, not just knocked out in one go.
Split the onboarding rewrite across a few hands - research the gaps, draft the fix, then have someone else check it before it comes back to me.
This is too much for one shot. Get it researched, drafted, and reviewed in stages instead of trying to answer it all at once.
I really like this expansion idea and that's exactly why I need someone to argue hard against it before I fall in love with it completely.
Poke every hole you can find in this hiring plan - I'm attached to it and that's the problem, so give me a straight yes or no at the end.
Before the board votes on this budget Friday, run it through the full gauntlet - facts, failure case, bloat, and whether the money actually works.
This restructuring plan needs the whole workup before I approve it: check the assumptions, find the failure mode, see if it's overbuilt, and stress the numbers.
I've got the leadership offsite Thursday and need the room, the agenda, and what outcome I'm walking out with.
Get me ready for tomorrow's quarterly review - what's the setup, who's in the room, and what am I trying to land.
I'm sitting down with Marcus Whitfield next week and need to know exactly what he's going to want from me walking in.
Before I call Deborah Ashcroft tomorrow, tell me what she's holding that I need and how she tends to push back.
Every month our invoice reconciliation eats two full days and half the time something's wrong at the end - I want to know why.
The onboarding checklist keeps producing the same three mistakes over and over and I want to know where it's breaking down.
The Tuesday deploy took down billing for four hours and I need an honest writeup of exactly what happened.
We shipped the wrong pricing to eleven customers last night and I need a straight account of how that got out the door.
Someone in the meeting kept saying 'attribution modeling' and I nodded along but I have no idea what that actually means.
What does 'burn multiple' mean? Just give me the quick version so I'm not lost next time it comes up.
I want to actually understand how our ad spend attribution works, not just the one-liner - walk me through it properly over a few sessions.
Sit me down and go through how cap tables work from the ground up, I've got time this week and I want it to actually stick.
Put together something clean I can hand Marcus summarizing where the partnership stands right now.
I need a one-pager I can send the board explaining why we're pausing the hire.
Write down how we close the books each month so Priya can run it without me walking her through it live.
I want the vendor onboarding steps captured somewhere so whoever takes this over next quarter doesn't have to ask me.
Just tell me straight - do we renew the Simmons contract or not, I've been sitting on this too long.
Give me a yes or no on the office lease. I need to stop going back and forth on this one thing.
I've got about nine things hanging over me right now and no idea which one to touch first - sort it out for me.
Everything's piling up at once. Tell me what actually matters this week and what can wait.
Okay so the lease is up, Priya's asking about her raise, the vendor thing is still unresolved, and I forgot to call the accountant back - just help me sort through all this.
I've got like six half-finished thoughts rattling around, some about hiring, some about the product, just catch it all and organize it.
I want to get us from where we are now to a working pilot by November - lay out the steps to get there.
Give me the path from zero to a hundred paying customers, in order, so I know what comes first.
Make sure this sticks for good - we never say 'affordable' in outbound copy again.
Going forward, log that Priya prefers async updates over calls, that's permanent from now on.
I'm out for the rest of today, jot down exactly where this build stands so tomorrow doesn't start from scratch.
Before I close this out for the night, capture what's done and what's still hanging so the next session isn't guessing.
